note: Re-judged 2026-10-24 (independent auditor, authored none of the change). RFC 7854 Section 4.9: "Reason indicates why the session was closed." 238bdb62e9 (spec-refuse-instead-of-defaulting) changed PeerInfo/StructuredEvent PeerAS from uint32 to rpc.RemoteAS; the unit now writes rpc.RemoteASOf(N) where it wrote N, the same known peer AS, and no assertion, input byte or expected value changed (TestHandleSenderStatePeerDown). The reason-byte assertions are unchanged. Verdict unchanged: enforced. Earlier judgement follows. Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after 4ef90497c6). Section 4.9: "Reason indicates why the session was closed." The earlier finding (no unit tied a Reason to the cause, and peerDownFor never emitted reason 4) is fixed and now proven at both decision points. Reactor: TestPeerCloseNamesTheTransportLoss drops TCP under a running Peer and asserts rpc.ReasonTCPFailure with Event 18; TestPeerCloseNamesTheCongestionTeardownLocal drives congestionTeardownPeer and asserts rpc.ReasonLocalClose with Event 18, so ze closing the transport itself is not reported as the remote doing it. BMP: TestRFC7854PeerDownTransportLossIsReason4 asserts Reason 4 ("This includes any unexpected termination of the transport session") with no Data for rpc.ReasonTCPFailure. TestHandleSenderStatePeerDown (reason 2 for a NOTIFICATION close with no cached PDU) and TestBMPSenderPeerDown (round-trips a chosen byte) remain weak on their own. Seam not covered by a tagged unit: apiStateObserver.OnPeerClosed and server/events.go copying the reason and CloseFSMEvent into the StructuredEvent. Single-polarity annotation holds: every Peer Down is written with a reason byte.
